text: {"thought": "The Period of Exchange and confidentiality dates are blank in the NDA text, so I need the minimum term rule to judge the duration. I look up P-10.", "action": "rule_lookup", "args": {"rule_id": "P-10"}}

{"thought": "The NDA excludes disclosures required by law (segment 35) but makes the notice steps apply first. I need the text of P-12, the notice-before-compelled-disclosure rule, to check it.", "action": "rule_lookup", "args": {"rule_id": "P-12"}}

{"thought": "No senior counsel precedent exists for this P-21 deviation with an employee counterparty, so I request approval from the General Counsel. Nothing is sent to the counterparty.", "action": "request_approval", "args": {"rule_id": "P-21", "reason": "The NDA with this employee is governed by Florida law, which deviates from P-21 (Ohio or Delaware) and needs General Counsel approval."}}

{"thought": "Segment 28 limits Confidential Information to technical information, which breaks P-13 for a partner. Segment 27 sets Belgian law, which needs General Counsel approval under P-21. Segment 18 gives a three-year term, below the 60-month minimum in P-06. Segment 22 includes a compelled-disclosure notice, so that rule is met. The findings are complete enough to finish.", "action": "finish", "args": {"findings": [{"rule_id": "P-13", "type": "violation", "evidence": [28], "explanation": "Partner NDA confines Confidential Information to technical information, excluding business and financial information. P-13 requires the definition not to be limited to technical information."}, {"rule_id": "P-21", "type": "approval_needed", "evidence": [27], "explanation": "Governing law is Belgian law with Brussels courts. P-21 requires Ohio or Delaware law unless the General Counsel approves another governing law."}, {"rule_id": "P-06", "type": "violation", "evidence": [18], "explanation": "The confidentiality term is three years. P-06 requires confidentiality obligations to last at least 60 months."}]}}

{"thought": "The DTSA notice is absent from the NDA, so the statutory risk applies. The governing law is English, which breaks P-22 and needs General Counsel approval. The duty of confidence is indefinite, which breaks P-11 (60-month maximum). I have the findings and finish.", "action": "finish", "args": {"findings": [{"rule_id": "P-22", "type": "approval_needed", "evidence": [14], "explanation": "The NDA is governed by English law. P-22 requires Delaware or New York law unless the General Counsel approves otherwise."}, {"rule_id": "P-11", "type": "violation", "evidence": [13], "explanation": "Segment 13 states that the confidentiality undertakings continue indefinitely. The maximum term is 60 months unless the General Counsel approves a longer term."}, {"rule_id": "LAW-DTSA-1833B", "type": "statutory_risk", "evidence": [], "explanation": "The employee NDA governs use of trade secrets but contains no whistleblower immunity notice under 18 U.S.C. 1833(b)(3). Without it the employer cannot recover exemplary damages or attorney fees under the DTSA against this employee."}]}}
